definition_zh: 观察；观测；观察结果；评论；（对规则的）遵守
definition_en: the act of watching something carefully, a recorded result of such watching, or a remark based on it
core_image: 一个人站在窗前，手里拿着本子，把鸟落下的时间一秒一秒写下来。
scene: 医生让病人先留院一晚，第二天早上再看检查数据。The patient stayed in the hospital for a night of observation.
sceneCN: 这里 observation 是“医学上的观察期、留观”（第 4 个义项）；句意：病人留院接受一晚的观察；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察；观测；观察结果；评论；遵守

senses.title: Watching with attention
senses.definition: the act of watching someone or something closely and with attention
senses.definitionCN: 密切而专注地注视某人或某事的行为
senses.example: Careful observation showed that the birds returned at the same hour each day.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细观察显示，这些鸟每天在同一时刻返回。
senses.why: Observation is not passive seeing: the watcher has chosen an object and a purpose, so attention is the defining element.
senses.whyCN: 观察不是被动地看见：观察者已经选定了对象与目的，因此“专注”才是定义性的要素。

senses.title: A recorded result
senses.titleCN: 观察结果：本子上那行字
senses.definition: a piece of information obtained by watching and often written down for later use
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察获得、常被记录下来备用的信息
senses.example: The notebook contained observations from six mornings at the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本里记着六个早晨在湖边的观察结果。
senses.why: Once written, the act becomes a fact others can read; the word then names the record rather than the watching.
senses.whyCN: 一旦写下来，行为就变成别人可读的事实；此时这个词命名的是记录，而不是“看”本身。

senses.title: A remark drawn from noticing
senses.definition: a spoken or written remark based on something noticed
senses.definitionCN: 基于所注意到的事情而作出的口头或书面评论
senses.example: His observation that the room felt colder was correct.
senses.exampleCN: 他说房间变冷了，这个观察是对的。
senses.why: The sense shifts from the eye to the mouth: a remark is called an observation when it reports a noticed fact rather than an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从眼睛移到嘴：当一句话报告的是被注意到的事实而非意见时，它就被称作 observation。

senses.title: A medical watch
senses.titleCN: 留观：先看着，等数据说话
senses.definition: a period during which a patient is watched in hospital before a decision is made
senses.definitionCN: 病人留院接受看护、等待作出决定的一段时间
senses.example: She was kept in observation overnight after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒后她被留院观察了一夜。
senses.why: Medicine uses observation as a treatment stage: when the diagnosis is still open, watching is safer than acting.
senses.whyCN: 医学把观察当作一个治疗阶段：诊断尚未确定时，看着比动手更安全。

senses.title: Keeping a rule
senses.titleCN: 遵守：把规定看在眼里并照做
senses.definition: the keeping or honouring of a law, custom, or religious practice
senses.definitionCN: 遵守或尊重法律、习俗或宗教实践
senses.example: Observation of the Sabbath was strict in that community.
senses.exampleCN: 那个社群对安息日的遵守很严格。
senses.why: The older sense of observare is to heed or keep; the same verb that means watch over also means keep faith with a rule.
senses.whyCN: observare 更早的含义是“留意、守护”；同一个既表示“看护”又表示“守信于规则”的动词。

senses.title: A post for watching
senses.titleCN: 观察位：专门用来盯的地方
senses.definition: a place, especially a military one, set up for watching an area
senses.definitionCN: 为监视某一区域而设置的场所，尤指军事用途
senses.example: The soldiers held the observation post on the ridge through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们整夜守住山脊上的观察哨。
senses.why: The act needs a place; when watching is continuous, the place itself takes the name and becomes part of the operation.
senses.whyCN: 观察需要地点；当观察持续进行时，地点本身也取了这个名字，成为行动的一部分。

senses.title: Studying from inside a group
senses.titleCN: 参与式观察：进去，同时记下来
senses.definition: a research method in which the researcher joins a group and records its life while taking part in it
senses.definitionCN: 研究者加入某群体、在参与其生活的同时作记录的研究方法
senses.example: Her participant observation of the night market lasted a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 她对夜市的参与式观察持续了整整一年。
senses.why: The method accepts a tension: to see ordinary life closely one must enter it, yet entering changes what is being observed.
senses.whyCN: 这种方法接受一种张力：要贴近看日常生活就必须进去，可一旦进去，被观察的对象也变了。

senses.title: Measuring the sky
senses.titleCN: 天文观测：把望远镜对准天上
senses.definition: the systematic recording of celestial objects and events with instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器对天体与天象作系统记录
senses.example: The observation of the eclipse required clear skies and an exact location.
senses.exampleCN: 观测这次日食需要晴朗天空和精确地点。
senses.why: Astronomy turns observation into data: the eye is replaced by a detector, and the record must state time, place, and instrument.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把观察变成数据：眼睛被探测器取代，记录必须写明时间、地点与仪器。

intro.en: Observation comes from Latin observatio, a watching or a heed, from observare: ob- 'over, before' plus servare 'to keep, watch over'. Servare also gives preserve, reserve, and conserve.
intro.cn: observation 来自拉丁语 observatio“看护、留意”，出自 observare：ob-“在上、在前”加 servare“守护、留意”。servare 还给出 preserve、reserve、conserve。

items.en: Servare meant to keep, guard, or preserve. The idea of keeping is older than the idea of looking.
items.cn: servare 意为保持、守护、保存。“守”的观念比“看”的观念更早。

items.en: Ob- added the sense of direction or attention: to watch over, to heed, to keep a rule, and to observe signs.
items.cn: ob- 增加了方向与注意的含义：看护、留意、遵守规则，以及观察征兆。

items.en: The noun covered watching, noting, and also compliance with a custom or a law.
items.cn: 该名词涵盖看护、记录，也涵盖对习俗或法律的遵守。

items.en: French kept both the watching sense and the remark sense, and English borrowed both in the 14th century.
items.cn: 法语同时保留了“观察”与“评论”两义，英语于 14 世纪把两者一并借入。

items.en: English observation grew in science and navigation, where watching had to be recorded with time and place.
items.cn: 英语 observation 在科学与航海领域壮大，那里的观察必须连同时间与地点一起记录。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries added medical observation, participant observation, and instrument-based astronomical observation.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪增加了医学留观、参与式观察，以及依靠仪器的天文观测。

note.en: The first group is the observe family; the second compares ways of gaining knowledge by watching, checking, or testing.
note.cn: 第一组是 observe 词族；第二组比较通过观看、核查或检验获取知识的几种方式。

entries.definition: to watch carefully, to notice, or to keep a rule. It names the action behind observation.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细观察、注意到，或遵守规则；命名的是 observation 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who watches, especially one sent to report on an event.
entries.definitionCN: 观察的人，尤指被派去报道某一事件的人。

entries.definition: quick to notice things; also careful to keep a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 善于注意细节的；也指谨慎守规的。

entries.definition: the keeping of a law, rite, or custom. It is the 'compliance' sense without the scientific one.
entries.definitionCN: 对法律、仪式或习俗的遵守；只有“遵从”义，没有科学观察义。

entries.definition: looking at something over time, often without a formal purpose. Observation adds method.
entries.definitionCN: 持续地看，常无正式目的；observation 则增加了方法。

entries.definition: continuous checking by instruments or staff, usually against limits. It is observation with a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 用仪器或人员持续核查，通常对照限值；是有阈值的观察。

entries.definition: the assignment of a number to a property. It turns observation into quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 给性质赋予数值；它把观察变成数量。

entries.definition: something said briefly. It need not be based on careful watching.
entries.definitionCN: 简短说出的话；不必基于仔细的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ob- 'over' plus servare 'keep'. Observation is keeping watch, and keeping a rule.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ob-“在上”加 servare“守护”。observation 就是守望着，也是守着规则。

normal.en: Observe means both to watch and to keep: the same act of holding something in view.
normal.cn: observe 既表示“看”，也表示“守”：都是把某物保持在视野里。

normal.en: An observation notebook is a watch that leaves a mark.
normal.cn: 观察笔记本就是一只会留下痕迹的表。

normal.en: In hospital, observation is a room where time does the testing.
normal.cn: 在医院，observation 是一间让时间来检验的病房。

normal.en: An observation post is the act of watching with a fixed address.
normal.cn: 观察哨就是有了固定地址的“看”。

normal.en: Astronomers write down three things: what, when, and with which instrument.
normal.cn: 天文学家记三件事：看到了什么、什么时候、用什么仪器。

abstract.en: Observation never arrives pure; the choice of what to watch is already a theory about what matters.
abstract.cn: 观察从不以纯粹状态到来；选择看什么，本身已是关于“什么重要”的理论。

abstract.en: The same verb means to watch and to obey, as if attention and loyalty came from one root.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既表示观看又表示服从，仿佛注意与忠诚出自同一根。

abstract.en: To observe a group closely is to change it; the observer is always part of the observed world.
abstract.cn: 近距离观察一个群体就会改变它；观察者永远是被观察世界的一部分。

examples.en: The ornithologist's observation of the nest lasted from dawn until the chicks fledged.
examples.cn: 这位鸟类学家对鸟巢的观察从黎明持续到雏鸟长出飞羽。

examples.en: After the head injury, the patient stayed under observation for twenty-four hours.
examples.cn: 头部受伤后，病人留院观察了二十四小时。

examples.en: Her observation that the machine ran quieter after warming up turned out to be important.
examples.cn: 她观察到机器预热后运转更安静，后来证明这一点很重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: observe（观察）+ ation（名词）——看得很仔细，还记下来，就是观察、观测。

root: 源自拉丁语 observatio（看护、留意、遵从），出自 observare：ob-“在上、在前”加 servare“守护、保持”。同一词根兼有“看”与“守”两面，因此既指观察、观测，也指对规则、习俗的遵守。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of observation, all descended from one act of keeping watch. The watch can be scientific, medical, military, or social; its product can be a record, a remark, a data set, or a habit of obeying.
sensesIntro.cn: observation 的八个义项都源自同一个“守望”动作。守望可以是科学的、医学的、军事的或社会的；其产物可以是记录、评论、数据集，或遵守的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a window with a notebook, writing down the exact second a bird lands.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗边的人拿着本子，记下鸟落下的那一秒。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS RECORD: watching with purpose, and the line written down afterwards.
branches.cn: 行为与记录：有目的地看，以及随后写下的那一行。

branches.en: WORD AND RULE: a remark drawn from noticing, and the keeping of a law or custom.
branches.cn: 言语与规则：由注意得出的评论，以及对法律或习俗的遵守。

branches.en: MEDICAL WAITING: a patient watched until the evidence becomes clear.
branches.cn: 医学等待：病人被观察到证据明朗为止。

branches.en: PLACE AND METHOD: a post built for watching, and a researcher watching from inside a group.
branches.cn: 地点与方法：为观察而建的哨位，以及研究者从群体内部观察。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTAL WATCHING: the sky recorded with time, place, and detector.
branches.cn: 仪器化观察：连同时间、地点与探测器一起记录天空。

intro.en: Observation is observe plus -ation, the action-noun suffix. The family adds -er for the person, -ant for the habit, -ance for the keeping of a rule, and -able for what can be seen.
intro.cn: observation 是 observe 加 -ation（动作名词后缀）。词族用 -er 表示人，-ant 表示习性，-ance 表示对规则的遵守，-able 表示可被看见。

latinIntro.en: The base is servare, to keep or guard, with ob- adding the direction of attention. Related Latin words give preserve, reserve, conserve, and servant.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 servare“保持、守护”，ob- 增加注意的方向。相关拉丁词给出 preserve、reserve、conserve、servant。

items.meaning: to watch closely, notice, or keep a rule
items.example: Scientists observe the same plot every spring.
items.exampleCN: 科学家每年春天观察同一块样地。

items.meaning: the act, result, or remark of watching
items.meaningCN: 观察的行为、结果或评论
items.example: His observation was recorded in the margin.
An observer sat at the back of the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 一名观察员坐在会议后排。

items.meaning: quick to notice; careful to comply
items.meaningCN: 善于察觉的；谨慎遵守的
items.example: An observant reader will spot the repeated date.
items.exampleCN: 细心的读者会注意到重复出现的日期。

items.meaning: the keeping of a law, rite, or custom
items.meaningCN: 对法律、仪式或习俗的遵守
items.example: Observance of the treaty was monitored by neutrals.
items.exampleCN: 条约的遵守情况由中立国监督。

items.meaning: able to be seen or noticed
items.example: The effect is observable only at low temperatures.
items.exampleCN: 这一效应只在低温下可观察到。

items.meaning: a place built for watching the sky or nature
items.meaningCN: 为观测天空或自然而建的场所；天文台
items.example: The observatory opens to the public on Fridays.
items.exampleCN: 这座天文台周五向公众开放。

items.meaning: to keep something safe from harm or change
items.meaningCN: 保护某物免受损害或改变；保存
items.example: The salt preserves the fish for the winter.

items.meaning: to keep back for later use
items.example: They reserved two seats near the window.
items.exampleCN: 他们预留了两个靠窗座位。

items.meaning: to keep from being lost or wasted
items.example: The town conserves water during dry summers.
items.exampleCN: 这个镇在干旱夏季节约用水。

definition_en: to watch something carefully, to notice, to make a scientific observation, to remark, or to keep a rule or mark a day

sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：为获取信息而长时间仔细观看；句意为天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、记录表、计时器、星图；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: To watch with full attention
senses.definition: to watch someone or something closely over time in order to learn how it behaves
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清某人或某物的行为而长时间仔细观看
senses.example: Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to watch over and heed, so sustained attention rather than a glance is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为看守并留心，因此持续注意而非一眼扫过，是最古老的一层。

senses.title: To notice
senses.definition: to see or become aware of something, often without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见或意识到某物，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: I observed a crack in the glass before it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃掉落之前，我就注意到上面有道裂痕。
senses.why: Attention can be caught as well as directed, so the same verb covers the moment something enters the eye.
senses.whyCN: 注意力既能被引导也能被抓住，因此同一个动词也覆盖某物进入视野的那一刻。

senses.title: To measure in a study
senses.definition: to record a phenomenon under controlled conditions as part of scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 作为科研工作的一部分，在受控条件下记录一种现象
senses.example: The team observe the cells every six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每六小时观察一次这些细胞。
senses.why: Measurement begins with watching, and science made the watching formal by giving it conditions and records.
senses.whyCN: 测量始于观看，而科学通过附加条件与记录，把观看变得正式。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something as a comment on what has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 就注意到的事情说一句话作为评论
senses.example: The reviewer observed that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人评论说样本太小。
senses.why: A remark is often the spoken form of something noticed, so the verb moved from the eye to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 评论常常是「注意到的东西」的口头形式，这个动词于是从眼睛移到了嘴。

senses.title: To keep a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, rule, custom or promise
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则、习俗或承诺行事
senses.example: Drivers must observe the speed limit near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在学校附近必须遵守限速。
senses.why: To observe a rule is to keep watch over yourself, the same inward attention the Latin verb first described.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是看住自己，正是那个拉丁动词最初描述的内在注意。

senses.title: To mark a day or rite
senses.definition: to celebrate or carry out a day, festival or ceremony in the proper way
senses.definitionCN: 以适当方式庆祝某个日子、节日或举行仪式
senses.example: The village observes the harvest festival every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子每年秋天都过丰收节。
senses.why: A custom is kept by being performed on its day, so the sense of keeping widened to the act of celebration.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠在其日子被践行而得以保持，因此「持守」之义扩展到庆祝行为。

senses.title: To keep someone under watch
senses.definition: to watch a person or place secretly, especially as part of an investigation
senses.definitionCN: 暗中监视某人或某地，尤作为调查的一部分
senses.example: Police observe the house from a van across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在街对面的货车里监视那栋房子。
senses.why: The same careful watching turns into surveillance when the watcher does not wish to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 当观看者不愿被看见，同样的仔细观看就变成了监视。

senses.title: To watch without interfering
senses.definition: in research, to study behaviour while taking no part that would change it
senses.definitionCN: 在研究中研究行为，同时不介入以免改变它
senses.example: The psychologist observes the class from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家在教室后排观察这个班。
senses.why: If the observer changes what is observed, the record is spoiled, so method demands watching with hands off.
senses.whyCN: 观察者若改变了被观察对象，记录就毁了，因此方法要求袖手旁观。

intro.en: Observe comes from Latin observare 'to watch over, heed', built on ob- 'over, before' and servare 'to keep, preserve'. The rule-keeping and celebration senses came through religious usage, and the scientific sense settled in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: observe 来自拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」，由 ob-「在……之上、在……之前」与 servare「保持、守护」构成。守规与庆祝两义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义则在十七世纪定型。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe, preserve or watch over, and it stands behind preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保全、守护、看守，preserve、reserve 与 conserve 都出自它。

items.en: The similar-looking servire meant to serve, and it gave servant and service; the two Latin verbs are different words.
items.cn: 形近的 servire 意为服侍，产生了 servant 与 service；这两个拉丁动词是不同的词。

items.en: Ob- plus servare made a verb for watching over something and attending to it, with attention as the core.
items.cn: ob- 加 servare 构成「看守并留心某物」的动词，核心在注意。

items.en: Old French observer carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of keeping a rule.
items.cn: 古法语 observer 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初意为遵守规则。

items.en: Observing the Sabbath and observing a fast fixed the senses of keeping a custom and of celebrating its day.
items.cn: 守安息日、守斋期固定了「持守习俗」与「在其日子举行」两种含义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy made observe a technical word for recorded watching, and observatory and observer followed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学把 observe 变成指「有记录观看」的技术词，天文台与观察者二词随之而来。

note.en: The first group shares the keeping root or looks close; the second group names ways of watching.
note.cn: 第一组共享「守护」词根或形近；第二组是各种「看」的方式。

entries.definition: The act or result of watching and recording.
entries.definitionCN: 观看并记录的行为或结果。

entries.definition: The person who watches, including the mere onlooker.
entries.definitionCN: 进行观看的人，也包括单纯旁观者。

entries.definition: Quick to notice details; also careful in keeping rules.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉细节的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rule or rite, not the act of looking.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或仪式的遵行，而非观看动作。

entries.definition: A building fitted for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的场所。

entries.definition: To keep safe from harm, from the same keeping verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 使免受损害，同一守护动词加不同前缀。

entries.definition: Work done for others, from servire 'to serve', not from servare.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人所做的工作，出自表示「服侍」的拉丁动词，而非表示「守护」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for looking at something over a period, with less formality.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指持续一段时间看某物，正式程度较低。

entries.definition: To become aware of something, without the suggestion of sustained study.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到某物，不含持续研究的意味。

entries.definition: To keep a continuous check, often with instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To look over a whole area or group, often to record its state.
entries.definitionCN: 遍览整个区域或群体，常为记录其状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the keeping verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of rules, rites and research.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「守护」动词、真实同族词，以及规则、仪式与研究里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin servare meant to keep safe, so observe is literally to keep watch over something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保全，observe 字面就是看住某物。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: observe a rule, observe a holiday, observe that.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：遵守规则、庆祝节日、评论说。

normal.en: Preserve and reserve share the keeping verb, while servant and service come from the serving verb.
normal.cn: preserve 与 reserve 共享「守护」动词，而 servant 与 service 出自「服侍」动词。

normal.en: An observatory is a building named for the watching, not for the stars.
normal.cn: 天文台是因「观看」而得名，而非因星星。

abstract.en: To observe a rule is to watch yourself as closely as you watch others.
abstract.cn: 遵守规则，就是像看别人那样看住自己。

abstract.en: The observer who changes the scene has already lost the thing worth recording.
abstract.cn: 改变场景的观察者，已经失去了值得记录的东西。

abstract.en: Attention is the whole word: watch, keep, and do not blink.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是注意：看着、守着、别眨眼。

examples.en: She observed the birds from the hide without making a sound.
examples.cn: 她藏在小棚里观察鸟，没有发出一点声音。

examples.en: Every driver must observe the signs at the crossing.
examples.cn: 每位司机在路口都必须遵守标志。

examples.en: The committee observed a minute of silence for the victims.
examples.cn: 委员会为遇难者默哀一分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽夫」——守在旁边盯住不放，看到什么就记下来：观察

root: 拉丁语 servare「保全、守护」→ observare「看守、留心」（ob- 加 servare）；经古法语 observer 进入英语。守规与庆祝义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义在十七世纪定型。注意与 servire「服侍」并非同词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pair of watching eyes: sustained attention, a sudden notice, a measured record, a spoken remark, a rule kept, a festival marked, a house watched in secret, and a class studied without interference.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一双观看的眼睛：持续注意、忽然察觉、有记录的测量、口头评论、被遵守的规则、被举行的节日、被暗中监视的房子，以及不干预地研究的课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on a hilltop a watcher holds a telescope on one star and writes its position every quarter hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶的观测者用望远镜对准一颗星，每刻钟记下它的位置。

branches.en: THE EYES: watching for a long time, and catching something in passing.
branches.cn: 那双眼：长时间的看，与路过时捕捉到什么。

branches.en: THE RECORD: cells counted every six hours, a class watched from the back without interference.
branches.cn: 记录：每六小时数一次细胞，在教室后排不干预地观察一个班。

branches.en: THE MOUTH: a note spoken aloud after the eyes have done their work.
branches.cn: 嘴：眼睛做完活之后，说出口的一句评论。

branches.en: THE KEPT RULE: attention turned inward, so that the driver watches himself.
branches.cn: 被守的规则：注意转向内部，司机看住自己。

branches.en: THE MARKED DAY AND THE SECRET WATCH: a rite performed on its date, a house watched from a van.
branches.cn: 被举行的日子与暗中监视：在正日子举行的仪式，与从货车里盯住的房子。

intro.en: Observe is a Latin verb of keeping watch, and its family split off from the separate verb meaning to serve.
intro.cn: observe 是一个表示看守的拉丁动词，其词族与另一个意为服侍的动词分道而行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is servare, ob-, observare and the noun observatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 servare、ob-、observare 与名词 observatio。

items.example: The verb keeps the image of a guard at a post.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留着岗哨看守的意象。

items.example: It also gives preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」「保留」与「保护」三词的来源。

items.example: It gives servant and service, and is not the root here.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「仆人」与「服务」两词，不是这里的词根。

items.example: It adds the idea of watching over something.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「看住某物」的意思。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its record.
items.exampleCN: 名词兼指行为与其记录。

items.example: The agent noun includes the mere onlooker.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词包括单纯旁观者。

items.example: The adjective also means careful in keeping rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也指守规谨慎的。

items.meaning: the keeping of a rule or rite
items.example: It names practice, not perception.
The suffix names a place of work.

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb servare (serv-, servatum; to keep)
latinEntries.example: Latin servare means to keep or preserve.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 servare 意为保持、守护。

latinEntries.example: Latin ob- appears in obicere, to throw against.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ob- 见于 obicere（扔向对面）。

latinEntries.example: Latin observare means to watch over, to heed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observare 意为看守、留意。

latinEntries.example: Latin observatio means a watching or a noting.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observatio 意为观看、记录。

definition_zh: 获得；得到；取得；赢得；（古）握有；（规则、习俗）通行
definition_en: to get or acquire something, especially through effort, request, or established right
core_image: 伸手向前，抓住一件东西并握牢
scene: 研究者在一间政府办事窗口等了两小时，就为拿到一张签了字的许可。A researcher waits at a government office window for two hours to obtain a signed permit.
sceneCN: 这里 obtain 是「取得、拿到」（第 2 个义项：通过努力或申请得到）；句意：研究人员在政府办事窗口等了两个小时，才取得一份签好字的许可证。图中可辨识物件：许可证、办事窗口、印章、签字笔、排号单；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 获得；取得；赢得
（规则、习俗等）通行；存在

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Take Hold: come to have something
senses.titleCN: 抓住：使某物归自己所有
senses.definition: to get or acquire something so that it becomes yours
senses.definitionCN: 得到或取得某物，使之归自己所有
senses.example: She obtained a copy of the report from the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 她从档案馆取得了一份报告副本。
senses.why: Latin obtinere joined ob- 'in front of' to tenere 'to hold'. The first sense is physical: you reach forward and close your hand on something, so obtain means to get it into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 把 ob-“在前”加在 tenere“握持”上。第一个义项是身体性的：你向前伸手，把东西握在手里，于是 obtain 意为“使某物进入自己的占有”。

senses.title: Earn the Hold: secure through effort
senses.titleCN: 挣得握持：通过努力取得
senses.definition: to succeed in getting something after effort, application, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力、申请或协商后成功得到某物
senses.example: It took three meetings to obtain the funding.
senses.exampleCN: 取得这笔资金开了三次会。
senses.why: A grip that must be worked for is still a grip. The hand reaches farther and closes later, so obtain adds the idea of effort to plain getting.
senses.whyCN: 需要费力才得到的握持仍然是握持。手伸得更远、合拢得更晚，于是 obtain 在“得到”之上加了“付出努力”的意思。

senses.title: Come By It: inherit or receive
senses.definition: in older use, to come into possession of something by inheritance or by receiving it
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指通过继承或受赠而占有某物
senses.example: He obtained the land from his father.
senses.exampleCN: 他从父亲那里继承了这块土地。
senses.why: The early French and Latin record lists 'inherit' among the senses of obtain. The thing still passes into your hold, but the reaching is done by family or gift rather than by effort.
senses.whyCN: 早期法语和拉丁语记录把“继承”列为 obtain 的义项之一。东西仍然进入你的握持，但伸手的是家族或赠予，而不是努力。

senses.title: Win the Field: obtain a victory
senses.definition: to gain or win something such as a victory, advantage, or right, often against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 赢得胜利、优势或权利等，常指对抗之中取得
senses.example: The small force obtained a decisive victory at the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小部队在隘口取得了决定性胜利。
senses.why: Early records also give 'conquer' as a sense. To obtain a victory is to take hold of the outcome after struggle, the same grip won against someone else.
senses.whyCN: 早期记录还给出“征服”义。obtain a victory 就是在争斗之后握住结果，是同一只从对手那里赢来的手。

senses.title: Hold Fast: the archaic sense of possession
senses.titleCN: 握牢不放：古老的占有义
senses.definition: in archaic use, to hold, keep, or possess something rather than to get it
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，指握持、保留或占有某物，而不是“得到”
senses.example: The old charter says the family shall obtain the manor for a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 那份古老契据说，该家族应握有这座庄园一千年。
senses.why: Obtinere in Latin could mean 'hold fast' as well as 'get possession of'. English kept the holding sense for a while: the hand is already closed and stays closed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 既可指“握牢”，也可指“取得占有”。英语一度保留了“握持”义：手已经合拢，并且一直不松开。

senses.title: The Custom Obtains: be current in practice
senses.titleCN: 习俗通行：在实际中成立
senses.definition: to be prevalent or customary, to be established in practice, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 盛行或成为惯例，在实际中确立，作不及物动词
senses.example: The custom still obtains in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然通行。
senses.why: From the 1610s the intransitive sense appears. A practice that 'holds' among people is one that grips the community, so obtain comes to mean 'be current'.
senses.whyCN: 不及物义自 17 世纪 10 年代出现。一种做法在人群中“握得住”，就是抓住了整个社群，于是 obtain 意为“通行、成立”。

senses.title: Obtain Permission: the formal request
senses.definition: to succeed in getting official permission, consent, or approval through the proper channel
senses.definitionCN: 通过正当渠道成功取得官方许可、同意或批准
senses.example: You must obtain written consent before using the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 使用这些照片前必须取得书面同意。
senses.why: Here the grip is granted by an authority. You put a request forward, the office puts a signed paper forward, and the paper passes into your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这里的握持由权力机构授予。你把申请递到前面，办事窗口把签好的文件递到前面，文件最终进入你的手中。

senses.title: Obtain Data: gather what is out there
senses.titleCN: 获取数据：把在外面的东西取回
senses.definition: to get information, measurements, or evidence, often by going to the source
senses.definitionCN: 取得信息、测量值或证据，常指到源头去取
senses.example: The team obtained samples from twelve different sites.
senses.exampleCN: 团队从十二个不同地点取得了样本。
senses.why: Data exist outside you and must be brought into reach. The old forward reach fits research: you go to the source, take the reading, and hold it as a record.
senses.whyCN: 数据存在于你之外，必须被带进可及范围。古老的“向前伸手”正适合研究：你到源头去，取回读数，并把它作为记录握在手里。

senses.title: Obtain a Degree: earn a standing
senses.titleCN: 取得学位：挣得一种资格
senses.definition: to complete the requirements for and receive a qualification, degree, or position
senses.definitionCN: 完成要求并取得资格、学位或职位
senses.example: She obtained her doctorate after six years of research.
senses.exampleCN: 经过六年研究，她取得了博士学位。
senses.why: A degree is conferred after requirements are met, yet it still enters your hold. The thing obtained here is a standing you can keep and carry.
senses.whyCN: 学位是在满足要求后授予的，但它仍然进入你的握持。这里取得的东西是一种你可以保有并带走的身份资格。

intro.en: Obtain entered English in the early 15th century from Old French obtenir or directly from Latin obtinere 'hold fast, get possession of'. The holding image in tenere is the core, and the intransitive 'be prevalent' sense followed in the 1610s.
intro.cn: obtain 于 15 世纪初从古法语 obtenir 或直接拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”进入英语。tenere 的“握持”意象是核心，不及物的“通行”义则于 17 世纪 10 年代出现。

items.en: Recorded as obteinen, meaning 'to get or acquire, inherit, gain, conquer'.
items.cn: 以 obteinen 形式记录，意为“得到或取得、继承、获得、征服”。

items.en: From Old French obtenir (14c.) or directly from Latin obtinere 'hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 obtenir（14 世纪），或直接来自拉丁语 obtinere“握持、握牢、抓住、取得占有、获得”。

items.en: Obtinere is ob- 'in front of' (here possibly intensive) plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: obtinere 是 ob-“在前”（此处也可能是强调用法）加 tenere“握持”。

items.en: Tenere is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch', the same root family as tenant and tenacity.
items.cn: tenere 一般认为可追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”，与 tenant、tenacity 同属一个词根家族。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'be prevalent or customary, be established in practice' is recorded.
items.cn: 记录到不及物义“盛行或成为惯例、在实际中确立”。

items.en: The verb yields obtainable, unobtainable, obtainment and obtainer. Its ob- prefix is shared with occupy (ob- + capere 'seize') and occur (ob- + currere 'run'), but the roots differ.
items.cn: 这个动词派生出 obtainable、unobtainable、obtainment、obtainer。它的 ob- 前缀与 occupy（ob- + capere“抓取”）、occur（ob- + currere“跑”）相同，但词根不同。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the -tain ending; the near-meaning group holds words that approach 'get' from different angles.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 -tain 结尾；近义组是从不同角度接近“得到”的词。

entries.definition: to hold inside. It shares tenere 'to hold' with obtain, but con- means 'together', so the holding is inward.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；包含。它与 obtain 共用 tenere“握持”，但 con- 意为“一起”，握持方向朝内。

entries.definition: to keep or continue to hold. The re- prefix points back, so the grip stays rather than being newly acquired.
entries.definitionCN: 保留；继续握有。前缀 re- 指向回，握持是留在手里，而不是新取得。

entries.definition: to reach or achieve. It looks like obtain but comes from ad- plus tangere 'to touch', not from tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它看起来像 obtain，但来自 ad- 加 tangere“触摸”，不是 tenere。

entries.definition: to get or come to possess something, often over time. It is more formal than obtain and stresses the process.
entries.definitionCN: 取得；逐渐占有。它比 obtain 更正式，更强调过程。

entries.definition: to get something useful or advantageous. It often implies an increase, while obtain is neutral about value.
entries.definitionCN: 获得（有用或有利的东西）。它常含“增加”，obtain 对价值是中性的。

entries.definition: to get something after effort and make it safe to keep. It adds certainty to the plain act of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力取得并确保保住。它在“得到”之上加了“确保”。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: ob- plus tenere 'to hold', the -tain family of contain, retain and sustain, and the fixed phrase 'the custom obtains'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：ob- 加 tenere“握持”、contain／retain／sustain 的 -tain 词族，以及固定说法 the custom obtains。

normal.en: Ob- 'in front of' plus tenere 'to hold' makes obtain: to get a hold of something.
normal.cn: ob-“在前”加 tenere“握持”构成 obtain：抓住某物、取得握持。

normal.en: Contain, retain and sustain all share tenere; only the prefix tells you which direction the holding goes.
normal.cn: contain、retain、sustain 都共用 tenere；只有前缀告诉你握持的方向。

normal.en: Obtain, occupy and occur share ob-, but their roots differ: tenere 'hold', capere 'seize', currere 'run'.
normal.cn: obtain、occupy、occur 共用 ob-，但词根不同：tenere“握”、capere“抓”、currere“跑”。

normal.en: Obtain permission is the standard formal frame for an official yes.
normal.cn: obtain permission 是取得官方许可的标准正式搭配。

normal.en: The custom obtains is the intransitive survivor: a practice holds among people.
normal.cn: the custom obtains 是不及物义的存留：一种做法在人群中握得住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching forward and closing around a handle; the handle is now yours to keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手向前伸出，握住一个把手；这个把手现在归你保有。

abstract.en: The same grip can be laid on a custom: a practice holds a whole community in place.
abstract.cn: 同一只握持的手可以放在习俗上：一种做法把整个社群握在原地。

abstract.en: At a counter, a signed paper slides forward into your hand: obtaining is that moment of transfer.
abstract.cn: 在办事窗口，一份签好的文件滑向前方、进入你手中：obtain 就是交接的那一刻。

examples.en: The laboratory obtained the samples from three rivers in the region.
examples.cn: 实验室从该地区的三条河流取得了样本。

examples.en: Students must obtain permission before filming inside the museum.
examples.cn: 学生在博物馆内拍摄前必须获得许可。

examples.en: That rule no longer obtains in most modern cities.
examples.cn: 那条规则在大多数现代城市已不再通行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额不，抬恩」——伸手一抬，把恩赐的东西接住 → obtain 获得、取得

root: 拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”= ob“在前”+ tenere“握持”（一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of obtain all keep one gesture: a hand reaches forward and closes. It can close on an object, a victory, a permission, a set of data, a degree, or even a custom that holds a community.
sensesIntro.cn: obtain 的九个义项都保留同一个动作：手向前伸出并合拢。它握住的可以是物件、胜利、许可、数据、学位，甚至一种握住了社群的习俗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching forward and closing on something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手向前伸出，把某物握在掌中。

branches.en: COMING TO HAVE: acquiring something, and receiving it by inheritance.
branches.cn: 归于己有：取得某物，以及通过继承得到。

branches.en: CONTESTED GAINS: securing something by effort, and winning a victory.
branches.cn: 争夺而得：靠努力取得，以及赢得胜利。

branches.en: HOLDING FAST: the archaic sense of keeping what is already in hand.
branches.cn: 握牢不放：保留手中已有之物的古义。

branches.en: HOLDING AMONG PEOPLE: a custom or rule that obtains, still current.
branches.cn: 在人群中成立：仍然通行的习俗或规则。

branches.en: FORMAL ACQUISITION: permission, data, and a qualification all pass into your hold.
branches.cn: 正式取得：许可、数据和学位资格都进入你的握持。

intro.en: Obtain is ob- plus the Latin root tenere 'to hold'. English adds -able, -ment and -er, while the same -tain root appears in contain, retain, sustain, tenant and maintain.
intro.cn: obtain 是 ob- 加拉丁词根 tenere“握持”。英语加 -able、-ment、-er，而同一个 -tain 词根出现在 contain、retain、sustain、tenant、maintain 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin obtinere 'hold fast, get possession' is ob- plus tenere 'to hold'. Tenere is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch'; it is not related to capere 'seize' or currere 'run', which build occupy and occur.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”是 ob- 加 tenere“握持”。tenere 一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”；它与 capere“抓取”、currere“跑”无关，后两者构成 occupy 和 occur。

items.meaning: to get a hold of; to acquire
items.meaningCN: 抓住；获得（ob-“在前”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: They obtained the land through a legal purchase.
items.exampleCN: 他们通过合法购买取得了这片土地。

items.meaningCN: 可获得的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The tickets are obtainable only at the door.
The rare mineral is almost unobtainable now.
items.exampleCN: 这种稀有矿物如今几乎无法获得。

items.meaningCN: 获得；取得（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: The obtainment of a visa took several weeks.

items.meaningCN: 获得者；取得者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The first obtainer of the map was a naval officer.
items.exampleCN: 第一个得到这张地图的人是一名海军军官。

items.meaningCN: 容纳；包含（con-“一起”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: The box contains old letters.

items.meaning: to keep or continue to hold
items.example: The soil retains water after rain.

items.structure: sus- (sub-, from below) + tain (tenere, to hold)
items.meaning: to hold up or keep going
items.meaningCN: 支撑；维持（sus- 即 sub-“在下”+ tenere）
items.example: The beams sustain the weight of the roof.
items.exampleCN: 这些梁支撑着屋顶的重量。

items.meaning: a person who holds a lease
items.meaningCN: 租户；房客（ten-“握持”+ -ant 表示人）
items.example: The tenant pays rent on the first day of the month.
items.exampleCN: 租户在每月第一天交房租。

items.meaning: to keep in good condition; to hold a view
items.meaningCN: 维持；保养；坚持（manu“手”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: The crew maintains the bridge every summer.
items.exampleCN: 养路队每年夏天维护这座桥。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；一目了然的；显眼的；（古义）常见的
definition_en: so clear or easy to see that it needs no explanation; standing openly in view
core_image: 一块石头正挡在必经之路中央，迎面撞上，想不看都难
scene: 从对岸都能看见坝体上的裂缝。The crack in the dam was obvious even from the far bank.
sceneCN: 这里 obvious 是「一眼可见、无法忽略」（第 2 个义项：显而易见）；句意：即使从对岸看，堤坝上的裂缝也一目了然。图中可辨识物件：坝体上的裂缝、渗出的水流、对岸的观察者、手中的望远镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 明显的；显而易见的；一目了然的

senses.title: In the way: the Latin core sense
senses.titleCN: 挡在路上：拉丁语的本义
senses.definition: in the literal Latin sense, placed directly in someone's path so as to meet them face to face
senses.definitionCN: 按拉丁语本义，指正处在某人前行的路上，与对方迎面相遇
senses.example: In Latin, an obvius thing was one that lay in your way and met you head-on.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，obvius 的东西就是横在你路上、与你迎面相遇的东西。
senses.why: Latin obvius came from obviam, 'in the way': ob 'in front of, against' plus viam, the accusative of via 'way'. The first picture is a physical obstacle standing in the road.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 出自 obviam“在路上”：ob“在前、迎着”加 viam（via“路”的宾格）。最初的画面就是一件挡在路中的实体障碍。

senses.title: Plain to see: impossible to miss
senses.definition: visible at once, without searching and without being told
senses.definitionCN: 一眼就能看见，既不用寻找，也不用别人告知
senses.example: The crack in the dam was obvious even from the far bank.
senses.exampleCN: 即使从对岸看，坝体上的裂缝也一目了然。
senses.why: Something standing in the road meets the eye before the mind has time to search for it. This is the 'plain to see' sense recorded from the 1630s.
senses.whyCN: 挡在路上的东西会在脑子来得及寻找之前先撞进眼睛，这就是 17 世纪 30 年代记录下来的“显而易见”义。

senses.title: Easy to understand: no explanation needed
senses.definition: so clear that the mind grasps it immediately, without a chain of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到脑子立刻就能抓住，不需要一连串推理
senses.example: The rule was obvious once the teacher gave a single example.
senses.exampleCN: 老师只举了一个例子，这条规则就变得明明白白。
senses.why: The road here is the road of thought: an idea that lies across the mind's path is reached without a detour, so understanding feels immediate.
senses.whyCN: 这里的路是思维之路：横在思路上的想法不必绕道就能抵达，于是理解显得毫不费力。

senses.title: Open and unconcealed: not hidden
senses.definition: not concealed or disguised; showing plainly what is actually there
senses.definitionCN: 没有隐藏或伪装，把实际存在的东西直接显露出来
senses.example: His disappointment was obvious to everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌边每个人都看得出他的失望。
senses.why: Latin obvius also meant 'open, exposed'. What is exposed is literally placed in front of the eyes, so there is nothing left to hide behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 还兼有“敞开、暴露”的意思。被暴露的东西就摆在眼前，已经没有可以遮挡的余地。

senses.title: The obvious choice: what anyone would pick
senses.titleCN: 不二之选：谁都会挑的那个
senses.definition: the answer or option so natural that no other seems worth considering
senses.definitionCN: 自然到让人觉得别的选项都不值一提的答案或选择
senses.example: For a first bicycle, the obvious choice is a small, cheap one.
senses.exampleCN: 第一辆自行车，明摆着的选择是买一辆小而便宜的。
senses.why: When only one option stands in the road ahead, it looks like the only road there is; what is plainly visible becomes what is expected.
senses.whyCN: 当前方路上只立着一个选项，它看起来就是唯一的路；看得见的东西于是变成了理所当然的东西。

senses.title: Barefaced: an obvious lie or mistake
senses.titleCN: 赤裸裸：明摆着的谎言或错误
senses.definition: used of faults so plain that no one could pretend not to see them
senses.definitionCN: 用于明显到谁也无法假装看不见的过失
senses.example: The excuse was an obvious lie, and nobody at the meeting believed it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个借口是赤裸裸的谎言，会上没人相信。
senses.why: A falsehood that stands in plain sight is shameless: the visibility itself becomes the accusation, so obvious adds contempt in this use.
senses.whyCN: 摆在明处的假话是无耻的：可见性本身成了指控，因此这一用法里的 obvious 带上了轻蔑。

senses.title: Obsolete: frequently met with, commonplace
senses.titleCN: 古义：常见的、司空见惯的
senses.definition: the earliest recorded sense, 'often encountered, ordinary', now no longer in use
senses.definitionCN: 最早记录的义项“经常遇到、平常”，今已不再使用
senses.example: Early writers used obvious for a sight so common that it drew no comment.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作家用 obvious 形容常见到无人置评的景象。
senses.why: A thing met again and again on the road stops being noticed at all. The 1580s sense was 'frequently met with', and modern English dropped that branch.
senses.whyCN: 在路上反复遇到的东西会彻底失去存在感。16 世纪 80 年代的义项正是“常常遇到”，现代英语丢掉了这条分支。

senses.title: Self-evident: true without proof
senses.titleCN: 不证自明：无需论证即成立
senses.definition: true in a way that needs no argument or evidence to support it
senses.definitionCN: 真实到不需要论证或证据来支撑
senses.example: The declaration calls these truths self-evident rather than proven.
senses.exampleCN: 宣言称这些真理不证自明，而不是被证明的。
senses.why: If a fact blocks the path of doubt, no proof is needed to get around it; the road metaphor turns logical and becomes self-evidence.
senses.whyCN: 如果事实挡住了怀疑的路，就不需要证据绕行；路的比喻转为逻辑意义，成为“不证自明”。

senses.title: The obvious: a noun phrase
senses.titleCN: 显而易见的事：名词性用法
senses.definition: used as a noun in phrases such as state the obvious, meaning what everyone already knows
senses.definitionCN: 用于 state the obvious 一类短语，指人人都已知道的事
senses.example: He kept stating the obvious: that the road ahead was flooded.
senses.exampleCN: 他不停地说显而易见的事：前面的路被淹了。
senses.why: English lets an adjective stand for the thing it describes. The obvious is whatever is visible to all, and saying it aloud is the fixed phrase state the obvious.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许形容词代替它所描述的事物。the obvious 就是所有人都看得见的东西，把它说出来便成了固定短语 state the obvious。

intro.en: Obvious entered English in the 1580s from Latin obvius, literally 'in the way'. The meaning 'plain to see' is recorded from the 1630s, and the old 'commonplace' sense has died out.
intro.cn: obvious 于 16 世纪 80 年代从拉丁语 obvius 进入英语，字面是“在路上的”。“显而易见”义自 17 世纪 30 年代有记录，而旧的“司空见惯”义已消亡。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'frequently met with, commonplace', a meaning that has since become obsolete.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是“经常遇到、平常”，此义后来废弃。

items.en: From Latin obvius 'that is in the way, presenting itself readily, open, exposed, commonplace'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 obvius“挡在路上的、自己送上门的、敞开的、暴露的、平常的”。

items.en: Obvius goes back to the adverb obviam 'in the way', built on ob 'in front of, against' plus viam, the accusative of via 'way'.
items.cn: obvius 出自副词 obviam“在路上”，由 ob“在前、迎着”加 viam（via“路”的宾格）构成。

items.en: Ob continues PIE *epi / *opi 'near, against'; via continues PIE *wegh- 'to go, move', the same root that gives way and wagon.
items.cn: ob 追溯到原始印欧语 *epi / *opi“近、对着”；via 追溯到 *wegh-“走、移动”，way 与 wagon 同出这个词根。

items.en: 'Plain to see, evident' is recorded from the 1630s, and this is the sense that modern English kept.
items.cn: “显而易见、明白”自 17 世纪 30 年代有记录，这正是现代英语保留的义项。

items.en: The visible branch survives in obvious, obviously and obviousness; the physical 'in the way' image survives separately in obviate and in the prefix ob-.
items.cn: “可见”这一支保留在 obvious、obviously、obviousness 中；物理性的“挡在路上”意象则另存于 obviate 和前缀 ob- 里。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to remove a difficulty or need in advance. It shares ob plus via 'way' and keeps the literal 'clear the road' image.
entries.definitionCN: 提前消除困难或需要。它同出 ob + via“路”，保留了字面的“清路”意象。

entries.definition: unaware of something happening around one. It looks close but comes from Latin oblivio 'forgetfulness', not from via.
entries.definitionCN: 对周围发生的事毫无察觉。它形似 obvious，却来自拉丁语 oblivio“遗忘”，与 via 无关。

entries.definition: feeling envy. It shares the -vious ending but goes back to Latin invidia 'envy', not to obvius.
entries.definitionCN: 嫉妒的。它同样以 -vious 结尾，但词源是拉丁语 invidia“嫉妒”，并非 obvius。

entries.definition: clear from the evidence available. It is more formal and often points to proof, while obvious points to the thing meeting the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 从已有证据看很清楚。它更正式，常指向证据；obvious 则强调事物自己撞进眼里。

entries.definition: seeming true from what is seen, which may or may not be the case. Obvious carries no such doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 从所见看来像是真的，但未必如此。obvious 不含有这层怀疑。

entries.definition: easy to see, hear or understand. It is broader and can describe sound and writing as well as sight.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见或理解。它范围更广，除视觉外也能形容声音和文字。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin parts ob plus via, the via family in deviate and previous, and the fixed phrase state the obvious.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + via，deviate 与 previous 中的 via 词族，以及固定短语 state the obvious。

normal.en: ob 'in front of' plus via 'way' gives 'in the way': the thing is standing in your road, so it meets you face to face.
normal.cn: ob“在前”加 via“路”就是“在路中”：东西挡在你的路上，于是与你迎面相遇。

normal.en: via, deviate, previous and trivial all contain via 'way'; obvious is the member of the family that stands in the way.
normal.cn: via、deviate、previous、trivial 都含 via“路”；obvious 是这个词族里“挡在路上”的那一个。

normal.en: The oldest sense was 'commonplace': something met on the road every day stops being noticed.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“司空见惯”：天天在路上遇到的东西，反而不再被注意。

normal.en: State the obvious is a fixed phrase for saying what everyone can already see.
normal.cn: state the obvious 是固定短语，指把人人早已看见的事再说一遍。

normal.en: Obviously and obviousness are the everyday adverb and noun built on the same adjective.
normal.cn: obviously 和 obviousness 是由同一个形容词构成的日常副词和名词。

abstract.en: Picture a road with one boulder in the middle: you do not go looking for it, it comes to you.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路中央横着一块巨石：不是你去寻找它，而是它迎着你来。

abstract.en: The same boulder can lie on the road of thought, so a fact, a lie or a choice can all be 'in the way'.
abstract.cn: 同一块石头也能横在思维之路上，所以一个事实、一句谎话或一个选择都可以“挡在路上”。

abstract.en: When nothing blocks the road, understanding is instant; when everything is on the road, the word slides into 'commonplace'.
abstract.cn: 路上没有阻挡时，理解是瞬间的；路上全是东西时，这个词就滑向“司空见惯”。

examples.en: It was obvious from the empty shelves that the storm had caused panic buying.
examples.cn: 从空荡荡的货架一眼就能看出，风暴引发了抢购。

examples.en: She made the obvious mistake of trusting a stranger with her luggage.
examples.cn: 她犯了一个明显的错误，把行李交给了陌生人。

examples.en: The solution looks obvious only after someone has pointed it out.
examples.cn: 解决方案只有在别人指出来之后才显得显而易见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，不喂我死」——哦，不喂我就要死，这么明显的事还用说 → obvious 明显的、显而易见的

root: 源自拉丁语 obvius“挡在路上的、迎面而来的”= ob“在前、迎着”+ via“路”，核心是“横在路上、一眼撞见”；更深的 *epi / *wegh- 为原始印欧语构拟。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of obvious all start from one picture: a stone standing in the middle of the road. The same obstacle then moves from the eye to the mind, to expectation, to shamelessness, and finally back to the oldest sense of 'commonplace'.
sensesIntro.cn: obvious 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一块石头立在路中央。同一个障碍随后从眼睛走到思维，走到理所当然，走到无耻，最后又回到最古老的“司空见惯”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone standing in the middle of the road, meeting you head-on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头立在路中央，迎面与你相遇。

branches.en: THE LITERAL OBSTACLE: the Latin thing that lies in the road and comes toward you.
branches.cn: 字面的障碍：拉丁语中横在路上、朝你而来的东西。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE: what stands in the open is seen at once and cannot be hidden.
branches.cn: 可见之物：摆在明处的东西一眼可见，也无从隐藏。

branches.en: THE CLEAR IDEA: the obstacle moves onto the road of thought, so understanding needs no detour or proof.
branches.cn: 清晰的想法：障碍移到思维之路上，理解不必绕道，也不必证明。

branches.en: THE ONLY OPTION AND THE BAREFACED: what is plainly visible becomes expected, and a visible fault becomes shameless.
branches.cn: 唯一选项与赤裸裸：看得见的东西变成理所当然，看得见的过失变成无耻。

branches.en: THE COMMONPLACE: what is met every day stops being noticed, and the adjective becomes the noun in the obvious.
branches.cn: 司空见惯：天天遇到的东西不再被注意；形容词也在 the obvious 中变成名词。

intro.en: Obvious is Latin ob- 'in front of, against' plus via 'way', with the adjective suffix -ous. English then adds -ly, -ness and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: obvious 由拉丁语 ob-“在前、迎着”加 via“路”，再加形容词后缀 -ous 构成。英语随后又加 -ly、-ness 和否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin obvius, from obviam 'in the way'; via 'way' is the noun at its centre.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 obvius，出自 obviam“在路上”；位于中心的正是名词 via“路”。

items.meaning: standing in the way, therefore plain to see
items.meaningCN: 挡在路上因而显而易见的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: The answer was obvious to the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 全班都觉得答案显而易见。

items.meaning: plainly; in a way that needs no explanation
items.meaningCN: 明显地；显然（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Obviously, the bridge is too narrow for trucks.
items.exampleCN: 显然，这座桥对卡车来说太窄了。

items.meaning: the quality of being easy to see or understand
items.meaningCN: 明显；显而易见（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: The obviousness of the error embarrassed the editor.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误如此明显，让编辑很尴尬。

items.meaning: not immediately visible or easy to understand
items.meaningCN: 不明显的；不易看出的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The link between the two events is unobvious but real.
items.exampleCN: 两件事之间的联系并不明显，但确实存在。

items.meaning: to clear a difficulty out of the way
items.example: A second entrance would obviate the need for queues.
items.exampleCN: 再开一个入口就不必排队了。

items.meaning: the act of removing a need or difficulty
items.meaningCN: 排除；预防（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The obviation of the old permit saved weeks of work.
items.exampleCN: 取消旧许可证省下了好几周的工作。

items.meaning: to move away from the road or the standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；脱离（离开原来的路）
items.example: The pilot had to deviate from the planned route.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员不得不偏离原定航线。

items.meaning: a departure from a route or standard
items.example: Any deviation from the recipe changes the taste.
items.exampleCN: 任何偏离食谱的做法都会改变味道。

items.meaning: going before on the way; earlier
items.meaningCN: 先行的；以前的（pre-“在前”+ via“路”）
items.example: The previous owner kept the keys in the shed.
items.exampleCN: 前一任房主把钥匙放在棚子里。

items.meaning: belonging to the crossroads, hence common and unimportant
items.meaningCN: 十字路口的，因而平常、不重要的
items.example: They argued over trivial details for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们为一个琐碎细节争论了一个小时。

latinEntries.meaning: in the way, open, exposed, commonplace
latinEntries.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；敞开的；暴露的；平常的

latinEntries.structure: via (noun, ablative viā also used as preposition)

latinEntries.meaning: to meet, to go against, to prevent

definition_zh: 明显地；显而易见地；显然；不用说；当然
definition_en: in a way that is easy to see or understand; also used to present something as clear from the facts or from common sense
core_image: 一件东西横在路中央，谁走过来都绕不开，也一眼就看见
scene: 教室的灯一亮，黑板上的错字立刻露了出来，门口站着的人都能看见。The mistake on the board was obviously a typo, and the teacher smiled.
sceneCN: 这里是「明显地、一眼可见」（第 1 个义项：以容易看见或理解的方式）；句意为黑板上的错误一看就是笔误，老师笑了笑。可辨物件：黑板、粉笔字、刚亮起的灯。

pos.zh: 明显地；显而易见地；显然；当然

derivatives.zh: obviously 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「明显的」

senses.title: In a way that is easy to see or understand
senses.definition: in a manner that is easy to notice, see or understand
senses.definitionCN: 以容易察觉、看见或理解的方式
senses.example: The road was obviously blocked by the fallen tree.
senses.exampleCN: 那条路明显被倒下的树堵住了。
senses.why: Obvious comes from Latin obvius, something standing in one's way, right in front of the eyes, so what is obviously true needs no searching.
senses.whyCN: obvious 源自拉丁语 obvius，指挡在眼前、迎面而来的东西；所以 obviously 描述的是不用寻找、抬眼就看得见的事。

senses.title: Used to state what any listener should accept
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to present something as clear from the facts or from common sense
senses.definitionCN: 放在从句开头，把某事说成从事实或常识看来很清楚的
senses.example: Obviously, a plan that costs nothing cannot build a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 显然，一个不花钱的方案是造不成桥的。
senses.why: Once a fact is placed right before the eyes, the speaker can invite the listener to see it too, which is how the word becomes a sentence opener.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事实被摆到眼前，说话人就可以请听话人一起「看见」它，这个词于是成了句子开头的引子。

senses.title: Used in speech to underline or agree
senses.definition: used in conversation to stress a point or to agree that something is plain
senses.definitionCN: 在会话中强调某一点，或表示某事明摆着、无需多说
senses.example: Obviously you must call before you visit.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，你来之前得先打个电话。
senses.why: In quick conversation the literal picture fades and the word becomes a nudge, telling the listener that the point is too plain to miss.
senses.whyCN: 在快速的口语里，字面的画面淡去了，这个词变成一个小小的提醒：告诉对方这一点太明显，不会漏掉。

intro.en: Obviously is the adjective obvious wearing the adverb suffix -ly, and obvious began as a picture of something placed directly in a road.
intro.cn: obviously 是形容词 obvious 加上副词后缀 -ly 构成的，而 obvious 最初画的是一件横在路中央的东西。

items.en: Via meant way or road, and it survives in English in phrases such as by way of.
items.cn: via 意为道路、路线，在英语里还留在表示「经由」的说法中。

items.en: Ob- plus via made obvius, literally in the way, and therefore standing before the eyes and plain to see.
items.cn: ob- 与 via 合成 obvius，字面是「在路上」，因此引申为「在眼前、一眼可见」。

items.en: English borrowed obvious for what lies in the way, is exposed to view and needs no explaining.
items.cn: 英语借入 obvious，指挡在路上、暴露在视线里、无需解释的东西。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the adjective settled into its modern sense of easy to see or understand.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个形容词固定为现代义：容易看见或容易理解。

items.en: Adding -ly created the adverb, whose sentence-initial use for it is clear that became common in modern writing and speech.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 造出副词，其中放在句首表示「显然、可以想见」的用法，在现代书面语与口语里都变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin words for road and for facing; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of clarity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「道路」与「迎面」之上的同族词，近义组收其他表示清楚的副词。

entries.definition: To remove a difficulty before it arises.

entries.definition: In a way that is easy to understand.

normalIntro.en: The word is a road with something lying across it: obvius means in the way, and -ly turns that picture into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一条路，路上横着东西：obvius 意为「挡在路上」，-ly 把这幅画面变成副词。

normal.en: Obvious comes from obvius, something that stands in the way, right before the eyes.
normal.cn: obvious 源自 obvius，指挡在路上、就在眼前的东西。

normal.en: Via is the Latin word for road, and obvius is what lies in the road ahead of you.
normal.cn: via 是拉丁语里的「道路」，obvius 就是横在你前头路上的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective obvious into the adverb obviously without adding a new meaning.
normal.cn: -ly 只是把形容词 obvious 变成副词 obviously，并不增添新的意思。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence, obviously tells the listener that the facts are already visible.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，obviously 等于告诉听话人：事实已经摆在那里了。

normal.en: In speech, obviously sometimes just means of course and carries a hint of impatience.
normal.cn: 在口语里，obviously 有时就是「当然」，还带着一点不耐烦的意味。

abstract.en: An object placed in the middle of a road needs no sign to be noticed.
abstract.cn: 一件横在路中央的东西，不需要竖牌子也会被注意到。

abstract.en: What is obvious is often obvious only after someone has pointed at it.
abstract.cn: 所谓明显，往往要有人指出之后才显得明显。

abstract.en: Repeating obviously too often makes the speaker sound as if the listener is slow.
abstract.cn: 把 obviously 说得太频繁，会让说话人显得把听者当成反应慢的人。

examples.en: The mistake on the board was obviously a typo, and the teacher smiled.
examples.cn: 黑板上的错误一看就是笔误，老师笑了笑。

examples.en: Obviously, a plan that costs nothing cannot build a bridge.
examples.cn: 显然，一个不花钱的方案是造不成桥的。

examples.en: Obviously you must call before you visit.
examples.cn: 当然，你来之前得先打个电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥伯维死理」——明摆着的事像死理一样不用争；记住 obviously 是显然。

root: 拉丁语 via（道路）→ obvius（挡在路上的、迎面可见的）→ 英语 obvious（明显的）+ 后缀 -ly → obviously（明显地）；同族词多与「路、迎面」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something lying in plain view; the senses divide into the manner sense, the sentence-opening assertion, and the spoken emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「摆在眼前、看得见」；义项分成方式副词、句首断言，以及口语里的强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single object lying across a road, impossible to walk around and impossible to miss.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西横在路中央，绕不过去，也躲不开视线。

branches.cn: 白板上一眼就看见的错字

latinIntro.en: Latin via and the adjective obvius supply the whole family, and obviam, the phrase for in the way, explains the picture inside the word.

definition_zh: 时刻；场合；重大活动；时机；机会；理由；原因
definition_en: a particular time when something happens; also a special event, an opportunity, and a reason or cause
core_image: 一枚怀表停在某个刻度上，指针正好落在值得记下的那一格
scene: 老钟表匠把怀表擦得发亮，说这块表只在最要紧的日子才舍得戴。He wore the old watch only on a special occasion, when the family gathered.
sceneCN: 这里是「场合、重大活动」（第 2 个义项：人们特意参加的重要活动）；句意为他只在全家团聚的特殊场合才戴上那块旧表。可辨物件：怀表、擦表布、老钟表匠手中的放大镜。

pos.zh: 时刻；场合；时机；理由

derivatives.zh: 由 occasion 加 -al 构成，义为「偶尔的；时不时的」
由 occasional 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶尔；有时」
由动词 occasion 加 -ed 构成，义为「由……引起的」

senses.title: A particular time when something happens
senses.definition: a particular point or moment in time at which something happens
senses.definitionCN: 事情发生的某一个具体时点
senses.example: On that occasion she arrived an hour late.
senses.exampleCN: 那一次她晚到了一个小时。
senses.why: Latin occasio named the moment that falls to a person, from a verb for falling, so the oldest layer is simply a point in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occasio 指落在某人身上的那个时刻，源头是表示「落下」的动词；所以这个词最古老的一层就是时间上的某一点。

senses.title: A special event or ceremony
senses.definition: an important event, ceremony or celebration that people attend
senses.definitionCN: 人们特意前往参加的重要活动、典礼或庆典
senses.example: The wedding was a grand occasion for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是全村的一件盛事。
senses.why: A moment that people mark, dress up for and gather around stops being mere clock time and becomes the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 当某个时刻被人们特意标注、盛装赶去相聚，它就不再只是钟表上的一点，而成了事件本身。

senses.title: A chance to do something
senses.definition: an opportunity or suitable moment for doing something
senses.definitionCN: 适合去做某事的时机或机会
senses.example: She took the occasion to thank everyone who had helped her.
senses.exampleCN: 她借这个机会感谢了所有帮助过她的人。
senses.why: If time can fall favourably into your hands, then that favourable fall is exactly an opening, which is why occasion also means opportunity.
senses.whyCN: 如果时间可以恰好落进你手里，那么这次有利的「落下」本身就是一道开口；所以 occasion 又能表示时机与机会。

senses.title: A reason or cause for something
senses.definition: a reason or ground for doing something, or a cause of an event
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的理由、依据，或某件事的起因
senses.example: There is no occasion for alarm; the test is only a rehearsal.
senses.exampleCN: 没有理由惊慌，这不过是一次演练。
senses.why: Latin occasio also carried the sense of ground or cause, and English kept it in phrases that ask whether there is any occasion for worry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occasio 还带着「依据、缘由」的意思，英语把它保留在问「有没有理由担心」这类说法里。

intro.en: Occasion is built on a Latin verb for falling: the word first named the moment that falls to a person, then the event, the chance and the reason.
intro.cn: occasion 建立在一个表示「落下」的拉丁动词上：这个词先指落到某人头上的时刻，再指事件、机会与理由。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it is the root behind case, accident and cadence as well.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下，也是 case、accident 与 cadence 的共同词根。

items.en: Ob- plus cadere made occidere, to fall down or fall upon, and also to happen or befall.
items.cn: ob- 与 cadere 合成 occidere，意为倒下、落到……上，也指发生、降临。

items.en: Occasio named the falling moment, the right time or opportunity, and also the ground or cause of an event.
items.cn: occasio 指落下的那一刻，即合适的时机、机会，也指事情的依据或原因。

items.en: Old French occasion carried the same set of meanings: time, opportunity and cause.
items.cn: 古法语 occasion 带着同一组意思：时刻、机会与原因。

items.en: Modern English keeps the time sense, extends it to important events, and still uses the word for a reason.
items.cn: 现代英语保留时间义，把它扩展到重要活动，也仍然用这个词表示理由。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin verb for falling; the near-meaning group collects words for moments, events and chances.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「落下」之上的同族词，近义组收表示时刻、事件与机会的词。

entries.definition: Happening from time to time, not regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 不时发生的，并非定期。

entries.definition: Sometimes, but not often.
entries.definitionCN: 有时，但不常。

entries.definition: An unexpected event that causes damage.
entries.definitionCN: 造成损害的意外事件。

entries.definition: A rhythm of rising and falling sound.
entries.definitionCN: 声音起落的节奏。

entries.definition: A very short period of time, or a particular point in it.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，或其中的某一时点。

entries.definition: A situation that makes it possible to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为可能的境况。

entries.definition: Something important that happens.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的重要事情。

entries.definition: A cause or explanation for something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的起因或解释。

normalIntro.en: The word falls out of the Latin verb cadere, and a moment that falls toward you becomes a time, an event, a chance and a reason.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁动词 cadere（落下）里长出来，而一个朝你落下的时刻，会变成时间、事件、机会与理由。

normal.en: Occasion rests on cadere, the Latin verb to fall, and means a moment that falls to you.
normal.cn: occasion 立在拉丁动词 cadere（落下）之上，指落到你头上的那个时刻。

normal.en: Occidere, to fall down, also meant to happen, which is why an occasion can be an event.
normal.cn: occidere 意为倒下，也指发生，所以 occasion 可以指一件事件。

normal.en: A moment that falls favourably becomes an opportunity, the third sense of the word.
normal.cn: 有利落下的时刻就成了机会，也就是这个词的第三个义项。

normal.en: The same Latin noun also meant ground or cause, so occasion can name a reason.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁名词也指依据、缘由，所以 occasion 还能表示理由。

normal.en: Occasional is the adjective for what happens only on some occasions.
normal.cn: occasional 是形容词，指只在某些场合才发生的事。

abstract.en: Time is not a flat line: some moments fall toward you and some slide past.
abstract.cn: 时间不是一条平线：有些时刻朝你落下，有些则滑了过去。

abstract.en: A special occasion is a day lifted out of the calendar and marked with care.
abstract.cn: 特殊场合是从日历里被拎出来、郑重标注的一天。

abstract.en: An occasion can be both the hour and the reason for gathering in it.
abstract.cn: occasion 既可以是那个时刻，也可以是让人聚到那一刻里来的理由。

examples.en: On that occasion she arrived an hour late.
examples.cn: 那一次她晚到了一个小时。

examples.en: The wedding was a grand occasion for the whole village.
examples.cn: 那场婚礼是全村的一件盛事。

examples.en: There is no occasion for alarm; the test is only a rehearsal.
examples.cn: 没有理由惊慌，这不过是一次演练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克神」——关键时刻像有神助；记住 occasion 是时机、场合。

root: 拉丁语 cadere（落下）→ occidere（落下、发生）→ occasio（落下的时刻、时机、缘由）→ 古法语 occasion → 英语 occasion；同族词 accident、cadence 也出自 cadere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a moment that falls; the senses run from a point in time to a marked event, then to the opening it offers, and finally to the reason behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落下的时刻」；义项从时间上的一点，走到被郑重标记的事件，再到它提供的开口，最后落到事情背后的缘由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watch hand stopping on one marked notch, the moment worth remembering.
core.cn: 核心意象：怀表指针停在某个刻度上，那一格正是值得记下的时刻。

branches.en: a late arrival still remembered years later
branches.cn: 多年后仍被提起的一次迟到

branches.en: villagers dressing up for a wedding
branches.cn: 村民为婚礼盛装

branches.en: a quiet hour opening for a word of thanks
branches.cn: 安静下来的一小时正好说几句感谢

branches.en: a doctor saying there is no cause to worry
branches.cn: 医生说没有理由担心

branches.en: a year-end dinner and the speech that gives it meaning
branches.cn: 年终晚宴，以及让这顿饭有意义的致辞

intro.cn: 这个词由表示落下的拉丁动词、由它构成的复合词、表示合适时刻的拉丁名词，以及两个分别造出形容词与副词的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 及其复合词 occidere 引出名词 occasio，而这个名词正是英语 occasion 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 偶尔的；间或发生的；偶然的；临时凑用的；不定期的
definition_en: happening or appearing from time to time rather than regularly, arising by chance, and made or kept for only a particular occasion
core_image: 一扇老木门整年关着，门轴上的灰积了薄薄一层
scene: 旧书店的卷帘门一年只拉起几次，门口的招牌褪了色，附近的人倒都记得它。An occasional customer still pushes the door open on Saturday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里的 occasional 是「偶尔的」（第 1 个义项：隔一段时间才发生一次）；句意为偶尔仍有顾客在星期六上午推门进来。图中可辨识物件：卷帘门、褪色招牌、门轴上的灰。

pos.zh: 偶尔的；偶然的；临时的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 occasio（时机、机会）经古法语进入英语，义为「场合；时机」
由 occasional 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶尔地；间或」
由 occasional 加 -ness 构成，义为「偶发性；不经常的状态」

senses.title: Happening from time to time
senses.definition: happening or appearing now and then, with gaps of time in between, rather than in a steady pattern
senses.definitionCN: 时而发生或出现，中间隔着一段段时间，而不是稳定持续地进行
senses.example: She made occasional visits to the village where she grew up.
senses.exampleCN: 她偶尔回一趟自己长大的村子。
senses.why: The Latin stem occasio named a moment that befalls a person, so an occasional event is one that only lands on certain moments instead of staying.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 occasio 指落到某人头上的某个时刻，所以 occasional 的事情只是在某些时刻落到眼前，而不是一直停在那里。

senses.title: Arising by chance rather than by plan
senses.definition: coming about because of chance circumstances, not because someone arranged or intended it
senses.definitionCN: 因偶然情况而发生，而不是有人安排或有意为之
senses.example: An occasional meeting at the station led to a long friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站的一次偶然相遇带来了一段长久的友谊。
senses.why: Since occasio could mean a lucky or unlucky turn of events, the adjective also describes what simply happens to us, without a plan behind it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 occasio 也可指运气好坏的一次转折，这个形容词便也能描述不由计划、只是落到我们头上的事。

senses.title: Kept or used only for a particular occasion
senses.titleCN: 临时的；应景的；备用凑用的
senses.definition: made, kept or used only now and then, for a special purpose, such as a chair set out when guests come
senses.definitionCN: 只为隔一段时间出现的特定用途而制作、保存或使用，例如来客时才摆出的椅子
senses.example: They kept an occasional table folded against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们家里有一张折叠着靠墙放的备用小桌。
senses.why: Furniture that comes out only on certain occasions took the adjective as a name, because the object leads the same intermittent life as the event.
senses.whyCN: 只在某些场合才搬出来的家具也用这个形容词命名，因为物件过着和「偶尔发生的事」同样断续的生活。

senses.title: Not regular in time or amount
senses.definition: not fixed to a schedule, so it cannot be counted on to appear at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定排期，因此不能指望它按固定间隔出现
senses.example: The clinic offers occasional free checks for older residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年居民不定期提供免费检查。
senses.why: Once a thing happens only on some occasions, nothing about it can be regular, so the word also denies a timetable without denying that it happens at all.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然只在某些时候发生，就谈不上规律，于是这个词否定的是时刻表，而不是它会发生。

intro.en: Occasional is an English adjective built on occasion, whose Latin stem names a moment that falls to someone; the whole family turns on the idea of something that arrives rather than continues.
intro.cn: occasional 是英语在 occasion 之上构成的形容词，其拉丁词干指「落到某人头上的时刻」；这一族词都围绕「降临而非持续」这个想法。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it is the source of many English words about things that happen, befall or simply drop.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下，是英语中一大批表示「发生、降临、跌落」的词来源。

items.en: Ob- plus cadere gave occidere, to fall toward or upon something, used of the sun going down and of events coming to a person.
items.cn: ob- 与 cadere 合成 occidere，意为「朝某物落下、落到某物上」，既用于太阳西沉，也用于事件临到某人。

items.en: Occasio named the moment when something falls into place, hence an opportunity or an occasion; it was also the name of a Roman goddess of the opportune moment.
items.cn: occasio 指事情正好落定的那个时刻，因此是「机会、场合」；它也是罗马神话中「恰当时机」女神的名字。

items.en: Old French kept occasion as a word for a chance, a cause or a particular time, and English borrowed it in that bundle of senses.
items.cn: 古法语保留 occasion，指机会、缘由或特定的时刻，英语把这几个意思一并借了进来。

items.en: English added the adjective ending -al to occasion, so occasional first meant 'belonging to an occasion' and then 'happening only on some occasions'.
items.cn: 英语给 occasion 加上形容词后缀 -al，于是 occasional 先表示「属于某一场合的」，后来才表示「只在某些场合发生的」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for a falling moment; the near-meaning group collects words for things that happen rarely or unevenly.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「落下的时刻」这一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示稀少或断续发生的词。

entries.definition: A particular time when something happens, or a reason for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的特定时刻，或做某事的缘由。

entries.definition: Now and then, at times that are not regular.
entries.definitionCN: 时而；不定时地。

entries.definition: A rhythm or flow, especially of sound or speech, from the Latin word for falling.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指声音或话语的节律，源自拉丁语中「落下」的词。

entries.definition: Something that happens by chance and is not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然发生、并非计划中的事；事故。

entries.definition: Happening only here and there, in scattered and unpredictable moments.
entries.definitionCN: 零散发生、时地不可预测的。

entries.definition: Stopping and starting again at intervals rather than running continuously.
entries.definitionCN: 时断时续，而不是连续进行的。

entries.definition: Not happening often, so that long gaps lie between the times it does.
entries.definitionCN: 不常发生，发生的间隔很长。

entries.definition: Not following a fixed pattern or timetable.
entries.definitionCN: 不按固定规律或时刻表进行的。

normalIntro.en: The word is occasion wearing the adjective ending -al, so every hook comes back to the picture of a moment that only sometimes falls into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 occasion 穿上形容词后缀 -al，所以每条记忆钩子都回到「只有某些时候才正好落定」的画面。

normal.en: Occasion is the noun behind the adjective, and -al simply means 'belonging to', so occasional belongs to certain occasions only.
normal.cn: occasion 是这个形容词背后的名词，-al 只表示「属于……的」，所以 occasional 只属于某些场合。

normal.en: Occasio in Latin was the moment something fell into place, which links the word to cadere, to fall.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 occasio 是事情正好落定的那一刻，这把它与 cadere（落下）连在一起。

normal.en: Occasionally is just occasional plus -ly, the plain adverb for now and then.
normal.cn: occasionally 只是 occasional 加 -ly，就是表示「时而」的普通副词。

normal.en: An occasional chair or table is an object kept for the times guests arrive, so furniture carries the same intermittent habit.
normal.cn: occasional chair 或 occasional table 是为来客时才用的物件，于是家具也带着同样「时有时无」的习性。

normal.en: In occasional showers, the adjective softens the forecast: rain will come, but not steadily.
normal.cn: 在 occasional showers 里，这个形容词软化了预报：雨会下，但不会连绵不断。

abstract.en: An occasional thing is defined less by what it is than by the size of the gaps around it.
abstract.cn: 偶尔发生的事，与其说由它本身定义，不如说由它周围的空隙大小定义。

abstract.en: Calling a moment an occasion admits that time is not a line but a series of landings.
abstract.cn: 把某一刻称作 occasion，就是承认时间不是一条直线，而是一连串的落点。

abstract.en: A word built on 'falling' reminds us that what happens to us often arrives rather than gets arranged.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「落下」之上的词提醒人：落到我们头上的事，多半是降临，而不是安排。

examples.en: He still makes occasional trips to the coast to fish.
examples.cn: 他仍偶尔去海边钓鱼。

examples.en: Occasional heavy rain slowed the harvest but did not stop it.
examples.cn: 偶尔的大雨拖慢了收割，却没有让它停下来。

examples.en: The spare room has an occasional bed for guests.
examples.cn: 备用房间里有一张供客人临时使用的床。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶开身」——身子偶尔才开一次门，平时都关着；记住 occasional 是偶尔的。

root: 由 occasion 加形容词后缀 -al 构成；occasion 来自拉丁语 occasio（时机、机会），其词干 occidere 意为「落到某物上」，再上溯 cadere（落下）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a moment that only sometimes falls into place; from it come chance happenings, objects kept for such moments, and the plain denial of a regular schedule.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是只有某些时候才落定的一个时刻；由此分出偶然发生的事、为这种时刻留着的物件，以及「没有固定排期」这一层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old wooden door that stays shut all year, with a thin layer of dust on its hinge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇老木门整年关着，门轴上积着一层薄灰。

branches.en: a shop door raised on a few Saturday mornings
branches.cn: 几个星期六上午才拉起的店门

branches.en: two strangers meeting at a station by luck
branches.cn: 两个陌生人在车站碰巧相遇

branches.en: a folding table kept against the wall for guests
branches.cn: 靠墙收着、来客才用的折叠桌

branches.en: a clinic with no fixed day for free checks
branches.cn: 没有固定免费检查日的诊所

branches.en: the same irregular rhythm seen in events and in services
branches.cn: 事件与服务中同一种不规则的节奏

intro.en: The word is a Latin moment-noun plus an English adjective ending; behind the noun sit a prefix and a verb of falling.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁语「时刻」名词加一个英语形容词后缀构成；名词背后还有一个前缀和表示「落下」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere, occidere and occasio are all recorded, and they give the family its picture of something falling into place at a certain moment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere、occidere、occasio 都有记录，为这一族词提供了「某物在某一刻落定」的画面。
